unit_description: This unit introduces equivalent fractions using models. Students understand equivalence as the same amount, find equivalent fractions using fraction strips and area models, and generate and explain equivalent fractions.
unit_goals: Understand equivalence as the same amount.
Find equivalent fractions using fraction strips.
Find equivalent fractions using area models.
Use models to show fractions that name the same amount.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students use fraction strips and area models to understand and generate equivalent fractions.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by shading two different models to show the same amount.
lessons.concept: Equivalent fractions name the same amount of the same whole. Even though the numerators and denominators are different, the shaded amount is the same.
lessons.practice: Identify and create models that show equivalent amounts.
lessons.objective: Understand equivalence as the same amount.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by matching equal amounts.

questions.hint: Both show half of the whole.
Both show the same amount of the whole.
2/3 is more than 1/2, 3/4 is even more; they are not the same.

learn.title: Equivalence as the Same Amount
teaching_points: Equivalent fractions show the same amount.
The numerator and denominator are different.
The whole must be the same size.

example.prompt: Show that 1/2 is the same amount as 2/4.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: Both are half of the whole.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Tell whether each pair of fractions shows the same amount.

bigIdea.title: Equivalence as the Same Amount
bigIdea.subtitle: Different names for the same amount
bigIdea.intro: Equivalent fractions are different ways to name the same amount. The number of parts and the size of each part change, but the total shaded amount stays the same.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why do equivalent fractions have different numerators and denominators?

ruleCards.description: Both fractions name the same amount of the whole.

ruleCards.equation: wholes must be the same size
ruleCards.description: Equivalent fractions only compare the same whole.

lessons.lesson_title: Find Equivalent Fractions Using Fraction Strips
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by lining up fraction strips of the same length.
lessons.concept: Fraction strips of the same length can be compared. When two strips show the same amount, the fractions are equivalent.
lessons.practice: Use fraction strips to find equivalent fractions.
lessons.objective: Find equivalent fractions using fraction strips.

questions.prompt: A 1/2 strip lines up with two 1/4 strips. What is equivalent to 1/2?
questions.hint: Two 1/4 strips cover the same length as one 1/2 strip.

questions.prompt: A 1/3 strip lines up with two 1/6 strips. What is equivalent to 1/3?
questions.hint: Two 1/6 strips cover the same length as one 1/3 strip.

questions.prompt: A 3/4 strip lines up with six 1/8 strips. What is equivalent to 3/4?
questions.hint: Six 1/8 strips cover the same length as three 1/4 strips.

learn.title: Find Equivalent Fractions Using Fraction Strips
teaching_points: Line up fraction strips of the same whole length.
Find which smaller strips cover the same amount.

example.prompt: Use fraction strips to find a fraction equivalent to 1/2.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Use fraction strips to find a fraction equivalent to 2/3.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Use fraction strips to find an equivalent fraction for each given fraction.

bigIdea.title: Find Equivalent Fractions Using Fraction Strips
bigIdea.subtitle: Line up strips that cover the same amount
bigIdea.intro: Fraction strips let you see that different fractions can cover the same length. When two strips match, they are equivalent fractions.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do fraction strips show that fractions are equivalent?

ruleCards.description: The strips must be the same total length.
The shaded parts cover the same distance.

lessons.lesson_title: Find Equivalent Fractions Using Area Models
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by shading the same area using different numbers of parts.
lessons.concept: An area model can be split in different ways to show equivalent fractions. The same shaded area can be called 1/2, 2/4, or 3/6.
lessons.practice: Use area models to find and show equivalent fractions.
lessons.objective: Find equivalent fractions using area models.

questions.prompt: A circle is shaded in 2 of 4 parts. What is an equivalent fraction?
A rectangle is shaded in 4 of 8 parts. What is an equivalent fraction?
A square is shaded in 3 of 6 parts. What is an equivalent fraction?

learn.title: Find Equivalent Fractions Using Area Models
teaching_points: Shade the same area of the whole.
Split the whole into more or fewer parts.
The fraction name changes, but the shaded amount stays the same.

example.prompt: Show that 1/2 = 3/6 using an area model.
example.equation: same shaded area, different number of equal parts

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Show that 2/3 = 4/6 using an area model.
try_it.hint: Shade the same area using 6 equal parts.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw an area model to show an equivalent fraction for each given fraction.

flashcards.title: Area Models and Equivalence
flashcards.instructions: Review area models and equivalent fractions.

bigIdea.title: Find Equivalent Fractions Using Area Models
bigIdea.subtitle: Same shaded area, different parts
bigIdea.intro: Area models help you see that the same shaded amount can be described with different fractions. When you split each part into smaller equal pieces, the total shaded area does not change.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does the shaded area stay the same when the number of parts changes?

ruleCards.description: Split each half into two fourths. Same shaded area.
The total shaded amount is the same.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by multiplying the numerator and denominator of a fraction by 2.
lessons.concept: You can generate equivalent fractions by splitting each part into more equal parts. Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number to find an equivalent fraction.
lessons.practice: Generate equivalent fractions and explain why they are the same.

questions.prompt: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 2. What is the equivalent fraction?
What fraction is equivalent to 1/3 when you split each third into 2 parts?
Multiply 2/3 by 3/3. What is the equivalent fraction?

learn.title: Generate and Explain Equivalent Fractions
teaching_points: Split each part into the same number of smaller parts.
Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number.
The new fraction names the same amount.

example.equation: 2/5 = 4/10 by splitting each fifth into two tenths

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Generate an equivalent fraction for 3/4 by splitting each fourth into 2 parts.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Generate an equivalent fraction for each given fraction and explain why it is equivalent.

bigIdea.title: Generate and Explain Equivalent Fractions
bigIdea.subtitle: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same number
bigIdea.intro: To make an equivalent fraction, split each part of the whole into more equal pieces. Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number. The amount stays the same.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number keep the amount the same?

ruleCards.description: Split each fifth into 2 tenths; numerator and denominator both ×2.
The total shaded area does not change.

lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: equivalence as the same amount, fraction strips, area models, and generating and explaining equivalent fractions.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.hint: One 1/3 strip lines up with two 1/6 strips.

questions.prompt: Generate an equivalent fraction for 2/5 by multiplying by 2/2.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: same amount + fraction strips + area models + generate = equivalent fraction models

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle shaded 3/4 is split into 8 equal parts. How many parts are shaded?

practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Equivalent Fraction Models
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: equivalence as the same amount, fraction strips, area models, and generating and explaining equivalent fractions.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about equivalent fractions with models?

ruleCards.description: Equivalent fractions name the same amount of the same whole.

ruleCards.equation: multiply top and bottom by same number
ruleCards.description: You can generate equivalent fractions by splitting each part into smaller equal parts.
